title: copilot tools / Choose and test a model
content: ## Choose and test a model **Get AI Model Guidance** supplies Foundry-oriented guidance for discovering models, preparing a deployment, and trying it in Toolkit. Describe your inputs, expected outputs, hosting requirements, and constraints rather than relying on a fixed default model. 1. Ask {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} to identify model options for the summarization task: ```prompt I am building a Python agent that summarizes support notes into three bullet points. Use Foundry Toolkit model guidance to help me choose a Microsoft Foundry model. Check the models already deployed in my selected Toolkit project first. Explain input limits and trade-offs I should test. Do not create Azure resources. ``` 2. Review the response. **List Microsoft Foundry Models** returns deployments in the selected project, not every model in the catalog. If you need another model, follow [model discovery and deployment](/docs/intelligentapps/models.md) and review availability, quota, and access before creating it. 3. Open your chosen deployment in [Model Playground](/docs/intelligentapps/playground.md#test-a-model). Test a short support note and a longer example with the same summarization instruction. 4. Check whether the response preserves important details and follows the requested format. Use [Compare](/docs/intelligentapps/playground.md#compare-model-responses) if you have multiple candidates. Record the deployment name you want the application to use. Model guidance is a starting point, not a benchmark or a promise about cost or quality. Verify the current model's capabilities and lifecycle, then test representative inputs. Playground comparison does not replace repeatable evaluation.
